📋 12 Entry Points

Surveillance

Disease Surveillance

Notifiable disease monitoring — avian influenza, BSE, foot-and-mouth, bluetongue, African swine fever. Real-time syndromic surveillance from veterinary reports. Wild bird surveillance for HPAI H5N1/H5N8. Sentinel flock and herd monitoring. Serological screening and PCR confirmation. Disease-free status under OIE/WOAH codes. Outbreak modelling with epidemiological contact tracing. Cross-border intelligence via EU TRACES and OIE WAHIS. Seasonal risk forecasting for vector-borne diseases. Rapid diagnostics pipeline from field to confirmed case.

Import

Import Controls

Border Target Operating Model (BTOM) for SPS checks. SPS certificate verification at border control points. Risk-based import categorisation (low/medium/high). IPAFFS digital gateway processing. Physical inspection scheduling at inland border facilities. Cold chain integrity verification for perishables. Third-country establishment audit trail. CHED processing. Emergency safeguard measures for emerging threats. Border Force and HMRC coordination.

Plants

Plant Health

Plant passport regime for intra-GB and GB-to-NI movements. Xylella fastidiosa surveillance and rapid response. Ash dieback monitoring and woodland management. Sweet chestnut blight containment zones. Oak processionary moth outbreak management. Phytophthora ramorum statutory eradication. Phytosanitary certificate validation. Protected Zone designations for quarantine pests. Seed testing and certification. Interception reporting from ports and garden centres.

Food Safety

Food Safety

FSA liaison for zoonotic disease intelligence. Salmonella, Campylobacter, E. coli O157, Listeria surveillance. AMR monitoring in food-producing animals. Food chain information from abattoirs and processors. Meat hygiene inspection and post-mortem data. BSE specified risk material controls. Food incident response with FSA and local authorities. Shellfish biotoxin monitoring. Radionuclide monitoring in food. Mycotoxin and contaminant surveillance in animal feed.

Livestock

Livestock Traceability

Cattle tracing via BCMS (CTS Online). Sheep EID movement recording. Pig identification and AMLS movement system. Poultry register and premises identification. Horse passport and Equine Database. Movement licence issuance and standstill enforcement. Birth, death, and movement notification. Cross-border rules under Windsor Framework. Livestock haulier biosecurity compliance. Market and gathering disease transmission assessment.

Laboratories

Laboratory Network

APHA Weybridge — OIE Reference Laboratory. Regional lab network (Starcross, Bury St Edmunds, Thirsk, Penrith, Carmarthen). Diagnostic capacity management for outbreak surge. Sample chain-of-custody from field to result. PCR, ELISA, virus isolation, histopathology automation. Turnaround monitoring (routine vs urgent vs statutory). EQA and proficiency testing. 7-day mandatory specimen retention. Biobank management for archived samples. LIMS integration across sites.

Wildlife

Wildlife Protection

Wildlife crime intelligence with NPCC-compliant handling. Raptor persecution monitoring (hen harrier, golden eagle, peregrine). Invasive alien species management (grey squirrel, signal crayfish). CITES enforcement for illegal wildlife trade. Badger sett survey and TB reservoir management. Bat protection during development works. Wildlife incident investigation. Non-native species licensing under Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981. Deer management and CWD surveillance. Avian botulism and mass die-off investigation.

Trade

Trade & Export

EHC processing via APHA online. Third-country equivalence assessment. SPS border checks under Windsor Framework and BTOM. Certification of animals and products for export. Bilateral veterinary agreements. Sanitary certificates for live animal exports. Phytosanitary certificates for plant exports. TRACES NT integration for EU consignments. Market access evidence and risk dossiers. FTA SPS chapter compliance.

One Health

One Health Intelligence

AMR surveillance across human, animal, and environmental domains (ESPAUR/VARSS). Pandemic preparedness with UKHSA and DEFRA CSA. Veterinary public health — zoonotic risk assessment. Wildlife-livestock-human interface monitoring. Emerging pathogen early warning. Cross-government One Health action plan. AMU reduction targets for livestock sectors. Environmental AMR monitoring in waterways and soils. Foodborne outbreak multi-agency coordination. OIE/FAO/WHO Tripartite.

TB

Bovine TB Programme

Annual tuberculin skin testing (4-yearly low-risk, 1-2-yearly high-risk). Gamma interferon ancillary testing. Badger vaccination in Edge Area. Licensed culling in High Risk and Edge Areas. Wildlife reservoir management. Cattle movement restrictions and trading rules. TB breakdown investigation with contact tracing. Pre/post-movement testing enforcement. Regional strategy differentiation (Low Risk, Edge, High Risk). Compulsory slaughter compensatory payments.

Analytics

APHA Data & Analytics

Caseload analytics across 12+ disease notification categories. Disease outbreak modelling (spatial epidemiology, R0). Surveillance data governance and sharing protocols. Performance metrics — sample turnaround, investigation closure. Livestock movement network analysis for spread prediction. Plant health interception trends by port. Import rejection pattern detection. Ministerial disease situation report dashboards. Open data for research and public transparency. Cross-system integration (BCMS, SAMU, APHA LIMS, IPAFFS).

Parliamentary

Parliamentary & International Reporting

DEFRA animal health statistics for PQs and select committee evidence. SPS policy impact assessments. OIE/WOAH WAHIS reporting. Disease outbreak situation reports to ministers. Annual reports on TB, AMR, plant health interceptions. Windsor Framework Joint Committee evidence. FSA annual report cross-reference. Science Advisory Council horizon scanning. Public consultation evidence for SPS changes. NAO readiness for animal health spending reviews.

⚡ 8 Transformation Priorities

1. Digital Disease Surveillance

Real-time notifiable disease detection from vet submissions, abattoir reports, and syndromic data. AI anomaly detection in notification patterns. Automated OIE/WAIS reporting. Wild bird surveillance with citizen science integration. Spatial epidemiology for containment zones. Target: 60% reduction in suspect-to-confirmed notification time.

2. AI-Powered Import Controls

Automated risk profiling in IPAFFS from historical compliance data. Predictive targeting of high-risk shipments for inspection. CHED processing with certificate cross-validation. Cold chain IoT deviation alerting. Third-country compliance scoring. Target: 90% of low-risk consignments cleared within 2 hours.

3. Plant Health Early Warning

Satellite and drone imagery for early pest/dieback detection. DNA metabarcoding of trap catches for rapid pest ID. Citizen science integration (TreeAlert, iRecord) for first-finder alerts. Climate suitability modelling for emerging pest risk. Automated plant passport compliance checking. Target: Xylella detection within 48 hours of introduction.

4. One Health Intelligence Platform

Integrated AMR dashboard across human (UKHSA), animal (APHA), and environmental (EA) data. Pandemic scenario modelling for zoonotic spillover. Automated AMU trend analysis linked to resistance patterns. Cross-domain risk ranking for emerging threats. Target: unified AMR data to all One Health partners within 24 hours.

5. Livestock Traceability 2.0

Single digital identity for every bovine, ovine, caprine, and porcine animal in GB. Blockchain-anchored movement recording. Real-time BCMS/CTS with market and abattoir integration. EID-based disease contact tracing in under 4 hours. Target: 99.5% traceability completeness across all livestock species.

6. Laboratory Automation

Automated sample registration from APHA LIMS. AI-assisted diagnostic interpretation for histopathology. Predictive capacity management for outbreak surge. Electronic result dispatch to submitting vets. Biobank automated retrieval and metadata management. Target: routine sample turnaround from 5 days to 48 hours.

7. Wildlife Crime Detection

Computer vision on satellite imagery for raptor persecution sites. Automated trap and poison detection from drone survey. NPCC-compliant intelligence sharing for wildlife crime units. Social media monitoring for illegal wildlife trade. DNA forensics automation. Target: 40% increase in prosecution rate within 3 years.

8. Trade Compliance Automation

End-to-end EHC digital processing. Automated third-country market access requirement checking. SPS certificate blockchain verification. Real-time export readiness scoring. TRACES NT bilateral integration for GB-EU trade. Target: 95% of EHC applications processed within 24 hours.

🚫 Red Lines (Never Crossed)

  • ❌ No disease notification delayed beyond statutory reporting timeframe
  • ❌ No SPS import check waived without documented risk assessment and ministerial approval
  • ❌ No wildlife crime intelligence shared without NPCC-compliant data handling
  • ❌ No laboratory sample destroyed without minimum 7-day retention and chain-of-custody record
  • ❌ No bovine TB test result overruled without APHA-approved veterinary second opinion
  • ❌ No antimicrobial resistance data published at farm-level granularity (herd/flock minimum)

🤝 5-Step Engagement Model

1
Discovery: Map APHA caseload across disease surveillance, import controls, plant health, livestock traceability, and wildlife protection. Assess laboratory network capacity (Weybridge + regional). Benchmark notification-to-confirmation timelines. Profile BTOM import compliance rates. Identify AMR data integration gaps. Map border control infrastructure and IPAFFS adoption.
2
Governance Design: Deploy DEFONEOS MCP servers against APHA use cases. Configure disease notification cascade, import risk profiling, and plant health early warning. Establish One Health intelligence framework with UKHSA and EA. Design livestock traceability digital identity architecture.
3
Pilot: Run 90-day pilot across 3 APHA regional offices and 2 border control points. Measure disease notification speed, import clearance throughput, and lab turnaround. Collect veterinary, trader, port health, and caseworker feedback. Benchmark wildlife crime intelligence sharing with NPCC.
4
Scale: Roll out across all APHA operations nationally. Integrate with IPAFFS, BCMS/CTS, TRACES NT, and APHA LIMS. Deploy across regional lab network and border infrastructure. Plant health early warning at all major ports. One Health platform operational with UKHSA and EA.
5
Assure: Continuous audit-grade APHA governance reporting. Disease surveillance dashboards. Parliamentary evidence generation. OIE/WAIS compliance tracking. Trade certificate KPI monitoring. AMR trend reporting. Wildlife crime outcome analytics.
